summary: POP attribute ontology covering core point/primitive/vertex classes, particle attributes, groups, dimension helpers, array attributes, and GLSL access idioms.

attribute_classes.name: point
attribute_classes.description: Point attributes are lists with one value per POP point. The built-in P attribute is the point position and most particle state lives on point attributes.

attribute_classes.name: primitive
attribute_classes.description: Primitive attributes are lists with one value per primitive, such as per-face Color or N data.

attribute_classes.name: vertex
attribute_classes.description: Vertex attributes are lists with one value per vertex across all primitives and are used when data must vary per vertex rather than per shared point.

P.planning_note: Treat P as the primary point position; generators and particle systems expect it to exist on point data.

N.role: Surface normal or direction vector associated with points, vertices, or primitives.
N.glsl_read: TDIn_N(), TDInPoint_N(), TDInVert_N(), or TDInPrim_N() depending on selected class
N.glsl_write: N[id] for selected-class GLSL POP or oTDPoint_N[id]/oTDVert_N[id]/oTDPrim_N[id] in GLSL Advanced POP

Color.role: Surface color and alpha, with RGBA values typically normalized from 0 to 1.

Tex.role: Texture coordinate attribute used for image and procedural texture mapping.

Weight.role: Point weight used by Field POP and masking workflows.

LineWidth.role: Per-point or per-line width attribute exposed as a predefined Attribute POP create option.

PartVel.role: Particle velocity in units per second.
PartVel.planning_note: Particle POP reads PartVel while updating P; preserve it in feedback loops.

PartForce.role: Cumulative particle force applied before the next particle integration step.
PartForce.planning_note: Force Radial POP writes or adds to PartForce, but Math Mix, Noise, Pattern, Lookup, and GLSL POPs may author it directly.

PartDrag.role: Particle drag factor used for deceleration during integration.

PartLife.role: Life expectancy name used by the general Attribute page point-attribute table.
PartLife.source_context: Attribute page point-attribute table lists PartLife, while Particle POP lists the particle lifespan attribute as PartLifeSpan.

PartLifeSpan.source_context: Particle POP names the lifespan attribute PartLifeSpan; the general Attribute page point table names the related life expectancy field PartLife. Keep both tokens searchable and verify the live operator build before normalizing user patches.

PartId.doc_conflict: Particle POP lists PartId as uint, while the Attribute page point-attribute table lists PartId as float. Prefer the Particle POP type for particle simulations and preserve the conflict note for live-build validation.

PartDeath.role: Optional particle-death control attribute used by Particle POP feedback workflows.

groups.downstream_scope: Group parameter fields on POPs restrict the operation to matching point or primitive groups when such groups exist.
glsl_notes: GLSL Copy POP exposes TDUpdatePointGroups() and TDUpdatePrimGroups() helpers for preserving input group membership through copy shaders.
Group POP sequential blocks can combine attribute, thin, pattern, group, and bounding logic; preserve block order when generating patches.

dimensions.scope: GLSL POP and GLSL Advanced POP dimension helpers map point indices to dimension coordinates and back.
dimensions.planning_note: Use dimension helpers when a POP represents grid-like or higher-dimensional point layout; do not infer 2D/3D coordinates from point indices without checking dimensions.

array_attributes.definition: An array attribute stores multiple elements of a chosen POP attribute data type per point, primitive, or vertex.
creation_notes: Attribute POP creates arrays by enabling Array and setting Array Size.
DAT to POP can collect similarly named columns into an array attribute when the column heading uses a name like MyArrayAttribute[3].
array_attributes.glsl_input_access: TDIn_AttribName(inputIndex, elementId, arrayIndex); arrayIndex is optional and defaults to 0.
array_attributes.glsl_array_size_constant: const uint cTDArraySize_Attrib for GLSL POP; GLSL Advanced POP uses class-prefixed constants such as cTDArraySizePoint_Attrib, cTDArraySizePrim_Attrib, and cTDArraySizeVert_Attrib.
array_attributes.planning_note: Prefer GLSL POP or GLSL Advanced POP when array attributes require per-element loops; Math Mix and Math Combine operate one array element per block in current docs.

planning_gotchas: Output attributes created or selected in GLSL POPs are allocated for writing; initialize every output element before downstream reads.
Guard compute writes with TDIndex() and TDNumElements() because dispatches can be rounded up to the workgroup size.
Attribute class matters: P on points, N or Color on vertices/primitives, and particle attributes are not interchangeable without explicit class-prefixed access.
Particle feedback loops must preserve reserved particle attributes and point counts unless Particle POP itself is responsible for birth/death.
